title: Playability report
description:
Whether a built game can be played and read by a first-time player, measured from outside: a bot drives the production build with real pointer and key input on desktop and mobile viewports, reads its play probe (shared/play-probe.schema.json) before and after each input, and inspects rendered frames. Every check names what was measured and the bar from the design's experience contract (core/reference/experience-rules.yaml) or core/reference/visual-quality.yaml. This is automation evidence: it proves the game is playable and visible, and it never stands in for what first-time players understand (a kill criterion measured from people).

Since 1.2.0 a check may be `SKIPPED`: the design does not claim the thing the check measures, so there was nothing to measure - a game with no win has no win.reachable to prove. A SKIPPED check is listed in `skipped_checks` with the reason and is never counted as a pass; a check that the design does claim and the build does not do is a FAIL, not a skip.

Since 1.4.0 every check names its `scenario` (`<check>@<project>`) and the report lists, per scenario, what the bot played for it - the bot version, viewport, policy and seed, the records with their sha256, the inputs and probe states those records list, and the frames - so a repair is verified only by a later measurement of the same check on the same viewport (docs/specialist-routing.md).

commit.description: The commit that was built and played.

measurement_class.description: Who played: a bot through the play probe. Never a first-time player.

projects.description: The viewports it was played on.

id.description: e.g. probe.present, start.objective, idle.grace, act.acknowledged, win.reachable, lose.reachable, restart.works, entities.visible, frames.luminance.

status.description: SKIPPED since 1.2.0: the design does not claim what the check measures, so nothing was measured. Never a pass.

summary.description: What was measured, and against which bar.

scenario.description: Since 1.4.0. The id of what was played for it in `scenarios`: `<check>@<project>`, stable across reports, so a later report's measurement of the same check on the same viewport is found by it.

frames.description: Captured frames, kept beside the run as evidence.

lit_share.description: Share of the frame's pixels lit (core/reference/visual-quality.yaml frames.lit_luminance).

records_dir.description: Since 1.1.0. The bot's raw records, relative to the run's directory: <records_dir>/<project>/<test>.json and <project>/frames/*.png - snapshots, entity samples (with each entity's asset and render), the requests for files under /assets/, and the DOM UI measured on each screen state. Later steps (production-quality) read them instead of playing the game again. Null when the bot never ran.

skipped_checks.description: Since 1.2.0. The checks that did not run because the design does not claim the thing they measure, each with the reason. A reader counting passes must subtract these, not add them.

reason.description: What the design does not claim, named: 'the design states no win condition'.

existing_content.description: Since 1.3.0. The existing-content floor counted on the shipped build through the probe (`source.method: probe`): written by the first visit that plays the adopted checkout's HEAD while the design's floor is `unmeasured` (the adopted checkout ships no content data file), and carried unchanged by every later report of the run - a floor once measured is never measured again. Absent when the run adopted nothing or its floor is counted on a content data file.

bot.description: Since 1.4.0. The bot that played: `version` is the sha256 of the bot (bot.spec.ts) as the step copied it into the clone, `settings_sha256` that of the settings it was handed (<records_dir>/settings.json). Two reports by different bots, or under different settings, measured the same check in different ways: a comparison between them is weaker, and is said to be.

scenarios.description: Since 1.4.0. What the bot played for each check, read from its own records (scripts/wgf_playability/scenario.py): nothing the bot did not record is added - a field it did not keep is null.

scenario.description: What the bot played for one check on one project.

viewport.description: The project's viewport; null for a check of the build rather than of a viewport (level.*: the commit's content data file).

policy.description: How the bot played the recordings the check reads: per recording (idle, each-offered-input, oracle, anti-oracle, ...), and naive play's seed and policies or risk's policies when the check reads them.

records.description: The raw records the check is judged on, relative to the run's directory, each pinned by sha256.

actions.description: The inputs the records list, in order, as recorded: the action, the input (pointer coordinates or key) when recorded, the time when recorded, the probe state before and after when recorded, and a count where the bot keeps only how many presses it made.

actions_complete.description: Every press the bot made for these recordings is listed one by one. False where it keeps only a count (the oracle's presses) or caps its list.

states.description: The probe state transitions the records list, with their times.

frames.description: The frames the check and its records name, each pinned by sha256.

omitted.description: How many actions, states and frames past the scenario's caps were left out.
